newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Aluminium perks up as guru talks bullish.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Aluminium perks up as guru talks bullish.

text.p: Aluminium prices headed higher on Monday after a respected U.S. industry analyst warned of a larger than expected supply deficit of the metal this year.
But elswhere commodity market made a quiet start to the week apart from coffee which continues very nervous in the wake of huge price swings in recent weeks.
Stewart Spector in his latest industry report said that aluminium producers were wary of restarting idled capacity too soon.
"It appears that major producers have finally learned their supply/demand lessons well,' Spector said.
The 1997 supply deficit could be around 835,000 tonnes because major capacity restarts now did not appear likely until the third of fourth quarter.
"These large producers are now significant net ingot buyers,' Spector said.

His report also pointed out that end-users of the metal widely used in transport, packaging and building industries, were running very low inventories and analysts at brokers GNI warned of the danger of using the "just in time" system of stock control.

"This reliance in 'just in time' stocks is very dangerous. The recent explosion in coffee prices has been because of JIT stock control - at some stage in the next two years aluminium will follow suit," GNI said.
Three months delivery aluminum prices on the London Metal Exchange reached $1,610 a tonne having languished below the round figure all last week.
London robusta coffee futures ended Monday at the day's highs with the July contract $67 above Friday's close.
Last week's sell-off probably shook a lot of the weaker speculators out of the market and those left in are probably there for the longer term, traders said.
"Nobody will be going short while we are in the Brazilian frost scare season," one trader said.

The precious metals sector was slow with traders awaiting for the next developments in the platinum group metals markets where Russia has been starving the market of its exports for most of this year, sending prices soaring.
Russia is the world's number one exporter of palladium and number two in platinum.
